findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: TagDevice now propagates the limit error to authentication, but tagDeviceUI still inserts the device into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains for 29 minutes. A second request with the same device ID hits the cache and returns nil, so Authenticate grants anonymous access despite the limit. Concurrent requests can bypass the check even before the first store call completes. Cache only successfully admitted devices, and ensure in-flight checks cannot be treated as successful admissions.

findings.title: Omitting the device header bypasses the configured limit
findings.body: Authenticate enforces the limit solely through TagDevice, but TagDevice returns nil without consulting the store when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, an unauthenticated client can omit that header and continue accessing anonymous APIs even when device_limit is exhausted. The configured limit needs an admission policy for requests without a device ID, rather than treating skipped tracking as successful admission.

findings.title: Device counting and admission are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices in one database session and performs the insert in a separate session without locking or another atomic admission mechanism. If the count is one below deviceLimit, concurrent requests for different new devices can all observe the available slot and all insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database, allowing the active device count to exceed the configured limit; subsequent updates continue admitting those excess devices. Serialize the count-and-admit operation at the database level and add a concurrent admission test.
